# Write a reviewer rule

A script rule (lawcheck docs concepts) can find `console.log` in a file. It cannot tell whether the message of `new Error('failed')` tells the caller what to do next. A reviewer rule (lawcheck docs concepts) can tell. With a reviewer rule, a language model reads each file against a rule (lawcheck docs concepts) you write in plain words. That model is the reviewer.

You end with a reviewer rule that judges `src/core/`. Lawcheck records the verdict (lawcheck docs concepts) of the reviewer in `.lawcheck/verdicts`. A later `lawcheck check` without `--review` reads that verdict in place of a call to the model.

The outputs below come from a repository whose `main` holds the `.lawcheck/` that `lawcheck init` makes. Its law (lawcheck docs concepts) has the type (lawcheck docs concepts) `library` that [Put the rule in the law](#_2-put-the-rule-in-the-law) shows, without the rule. On a branch made from `main`, you added `src/core/refund.ts`:

```ts
export function refund(paid: boolean): number {
  if (!paid) throw new Error('failed');
  return 1;
}
```

A test server that answers as Ollama does gave the answers below. A real model words its findings (lawcheck docs concepts) in its own way.

## 1. Write the rule file

`init` makes no `rules/` folder. Create it with `mkdir -p .lawcheck/rules`, then write the file `.lawcheck/rules/clear-errors.md`. It says what must hold, what to report, and what does not count:

```text
Every error message a caller can see says what happened and what the caller can do next.

Report each thrown error or returned error message that leaves one of the two out. A message logged for developers is not such a message.
```

The reviewer receives this text, the rule's `why` and the file it judges.

## 2. Put the rule in the law

Give the rule a `why`. List the rule on the type. The reviewer may need another file beside the file it judges, such as a catalogue of messages. In that case, list the file under the `context` key of the rule (Reviewer rules (lawcheck docs reviewer-rules)). Write `.lawcheck/law.yaml`:

```yaml
lawcheck: 0.1.0

rules:
  clear-errors:
    why: An error a caller sees says what happened and what to do next.

types:
  library:
    about: Code the commands call.
    paths: ["src/core/**"]
    rules: [clear-errors]
```

## 3. Choose a reviewer

| You have | `provider` | Key |
|---|---|---|
| an API key of Anthropic, OpenAI or Google | `anthropic`, `openai` or `google` | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY` or `GOOGLE_API_KEY` in the environment |
| a model on your own machine, served by Ollama | `ollama` | none |
| another server that answers chat completions as OpenAI does | `openai-compatible`, with its address in `LAWCHECK_REVIEWER_ENDPOINT` | `LAWCHECK_REVIEWER_KEY` in the environment, when the server needs a key |
| Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI or Copilot CLI, signed in | `claude-code`, `codex`, `gemini-cli` or `copilot-cli` | the program's own sign-in |

These steps use Ollama. Lawcheck calls it on `localhost:11434`, or at the address in `LAWCHECK_REVIEWER_ENDPOINT`. Create `.lawcheck/config.yaml`, with the name of a model the server has pulled:

```yaml
reviewer:
  provider: ollama
  model: your-model-id
```

A key goes in the environment, because Lawcheck refuses a key in this file with `config-invalid` (lawcheck docs codes). Reviewers and keys (lawcheck docs providers) has every provider and its keys.

## 4. Check that the reviewer answers

```text
$ lawcheck doctor --reviewer
```

`doctor` sends the reviewer one small request. The last line of its output is:

```output
ok  reviewer  1 reviewer rule; ollama answered a test call
```

A plain check (lawcheck docs concepts) reads the pass from `.lawcheck/verdicts`. It calls no model. A CI job runs the same plain check with no key (CI and git hooks (lawcheck docs ci)).

## If it goes wrong

- Lawcheck prints `reviewer-unreachable` (lawcheck docs codes): the server is down, the key is wrong, or the program is not signed in. The message names the cause. Fix the cause and run the same command again. `check --review` keeps the answers it got before the failure, so the second run asks the reviewer only about the

files it has no answer for.
- The reviewer failed a file you believe is right. Lawcheck keeps the fail on this machine. It shows the fail again without a call, until the file or the rule changes. With `--again`, Lawcheck asks the reviewer once more: `lawcheck check --review --again --base main`.
- Lawcheck prints `too-large-to-review` (lawcheck docs codes): the prompt of a file holds more characters than the setting `reviewer.max_chars` allows. Its default is 50,000. Lawcheck never sends such a prompt. Split the file, or raise `max_chars` in `.lawcheck/config.yaml`.
- Lawcheck prints `reviewer-bad-answer` (lawcheck docs codes): the model gave no verdict twice. Reword the rule file, or try another model.
- Lawcheck prints `too-many-reviews` (lawcheck docs codes): the run needs more calls than the setting `reviewer.max_calls` allows (100 by default). Lawcheck then makes none of them. A slow check (lawcheck docs slow-check) shows how to cap the calls.
- Lawcheck keeps every recorded pass after you change the model or the provider. It records a pass under a key made from the file and the rule. The key holds no provider and no model. Check the new setup with `lawcheck doctor --reviewer`.
